boxes.observation: The initial capital is I. Its uppermost horizontal stroke has an apparent right arrowhead; plain overbar remains possible. The first word is read tentatively as trièdre. The last word is most likely orienté, but unité remains a local alternative. A small clipped curved ink fragment touches the top crop boundary and cannot be assigned a complete character from this rectangle.

Q is secure. The strokes above it are densely retraced, with two horizontal levels and oblique joining strokes. A cancelled arrow over Q is one possible reading; a single retraced right arrow is the alternative. Q itself is not visibly struck through.
Orienté is crossed out by a horizontal stroke; the final acute accent remains visible.

An R-shaped upper bowl, left stem and diagonal leg overlap a large rounded Q-like outline. Q overwritten by R is the primary tentative interpretation; an unusually retraced R is the alternative. The upper mark is read as a bar, though its right end is heavily inked.
Horizontal cancellation spans both words. Face is readable; par is tentative, especially its first descending letter and final strokes.
Capital H has a strongly ascending diagonal cross stroke. The separate-looking top horizontal mark is read as an overbar, with a right arrow as alternative.
Pair (1,1). A short cropped stroke touches the left boundary beside the opening parenthesis; no complete preceding symbol is inferred.
Pair (0,5). The upper stroke of 5 is detached from its lower stroke.
Pair (1,2); the second numeral is visibly higher than the first and has been raised typographically without assigning it an exponent role.

unresolved: B025-01: accent above I and wording have local alternatives.
B025-02: whether the dense upper strokes cancel an arrow is uncertain.
B025-04: Q-to-R overwriting versus retraced R is uncertain.
B025-05: final struck-out word tentatively par.
excluded: Paper marks, specks and reverse-side show-through were not transcribed; no text beyond the assigned rectangles was supplied.
